Tier-1 evidence in [UIAO_131 §3.1](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/specs/adapter-test-strategy.md) requires a live commercial-cloud tenant for the adapter under test. The substrate has none of its own — UIAO lives outside any tenant boundary. Each contributor brings their own.

This page is the opinionated setup for the **recommended first target: the Microsoft 365 Developer Program**. It's free, it ships with Entra ID P2, and it gives you enough scope to exercise the `entra-id`, `m365`, and `scuba`-family adapters (the three highest-priority adapters in the [Substrate Status test-tier table](../docs/substrate-status.html)).

::: {.callout-warning}
## Commercial cloud, not GCC-Moderate
The Developer Program tenant is **WW Commercial cloud**. Tests against it validate common-plane adapter logic, not GCC-Moderate-specific behavior. For the GCC-Moderate side — including the documented [FINDING-001 INR unavailability](../findings/fedramp-gcc-moderate-informed-network-routing.html) — you record tier-2 contract fixtures from Microsoft Learn sources, not from this tenant. If you have authorized access to an agency-provided GCC-Moderate tenant, see [Using a Federal GCC-Moderate tenant](#using-a-federal-gcc-moderate-tenant) below.
:::

## Prerequisites

- A Microsoft account (personal, work, or dedicated UIAO-contributor account). If you use a work account, confirm with your employer that test-tenant sign-up is permitted under their policy.
- Approximately **15 minutes** for first-time sign-up.
- PowerShell 7+ or Python 3.10+ on your workstation (for running adapter code).

## Step 1 — Create the developer tenant

1. Go to the Microsoft 365 Developer Program: **`https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/dev-program`** ([Microsoft Learn FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/developer-program/microsoft-365-developer-program-faq) for program details).

2. Sign in with your Microsoft account. Complete the profile:
   - Region
   - Company name (your own is fine)
   - Developer interests (pick Microsoft 365 + Identity + Security)

3. Click **"Set up subscription"**. Choose one:
   - **Instant sandbox** — pre-provisioned with Teams, SharePoint, Outlook, Office, and 24 test users + 1 admin. Recommended for first-time contributors.
   - **Configurable sandbox** — blank slate; you provision users and data yourself.

4. Pick a domain name (`.onmicrosoft.com`) and set the initial admin password. **Save both somewhere encrypted** — you'll use these for every test run.

5. Wait ~5 minutes. Microsoft provisions the tenant and emails confirmation.

**Verify:** you can sign in at `https://admin.microsoft.com` with the admin account. The admin center shows 25 E5 licenses including Entra ID P2.

## Step 2 — Register an app for adapter authentication

UIAO adapters authenticate to M365/Entra via an **app registration** using the client-credentials OAuth flow.

1. In the Entra admin center (`https://entra.microsoft.com`), go to **Applications → App registrations → New registration**.
2. Name: `UIAO-Adapter-Test` (or similar — use a name that identifies this as test-environment credentials).
3. Supported account types: **Accounts in this organizational directory only** (Single tenant).
4. Redirect URI: leave blank.
5. Create.
6. On the new app's overview page, copy and save (encrypted):
   - **Application (client) ID**
   - **Directory (tenant) ID**

## Step 3 — Grant API permissions

The adapter needs read permissions on Microsoft Graph (and, for `scuba`, the Office 365 Management APIs).

1. App registration → **API permissions → Add a permission → Microsoft Graph → Application permissions**.
2. Add (at minimum): `Directory.Read.All`, `Policy.Read.All`, `User.Read.All`, `Group.Read.All`, `AuditLog.Read.All`.
3. For `scuba` adapter testing: add **Office 365 Management APIs → Application → ServiceHealth.Read**.
4. Click **Grant admin consent for <your-tenant>**. Confirm.

## Step 4 — Create a client secret

1. App registration → **Certificates & secrets → New client secret**.
2. Description: `UIAO adapter test secret`. Expiry: 90 days (match the developer-tenant renewal cycle).
3. **Copy the secret value immediately** — it is displayed exactly once. Save encrypted.

## Step 5 — Store credentials

The substrate never commits credentials. Store them in an environment that only your workstation can see:

```powershell
# PowerShell (per-session)
$env:UIAO_TEST_TENANT_ID   = "<directory-id>"
$env:UIAO_TEST_CLIENT_ID   = "<application-id>"
$env:UIAO_TEST_CLIENT_SECRET = "<client-secret-value>"
```

```bash
# Bash (add to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc — consider a password manager instead)
export UIAO_TEST_TENANT_ID="<directory-id>"
export UIAO_TEST_CLIENT_ID="<application-id>"
export UIAO_TEST_CLIENT_SECRET="<client-secret-value>"
```

A credentials-from-file pattern (`.env` loaded via `python-dotenv` or similar) is also fine. **Never** commit any file containing the secret value, even in `inbox/` — the `.gitignore` won't save you from a `git add -f`.

## Step 6 — Verify the token flow

Confirm the app can issue a Graph token:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://login.microsoftonline.com/$UIAO_TEST_TENANT_ID/oauth2/v2.0/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "client_id=$UIAO_TEST_CLIENT_ID" \
  -d "client_secret=$UIAO_TEST_CLIENT_SECRET" \
  -d "scope=https://graph.microsoft.com/.default" \
  -d "grant_type=client_credentials"
```

**Verify:** returns `{ "access_token": "...", "expires_in": 3599, ... }`. Copy `access_token` and test one Graph call:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>" \
  "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/organization"
```

If both return 200 OK, your tenant + app + permissions + secret are wired correctly. You're ready to run adapter tests.

## Step 7 — Record your first tier-1 evidence

From the repo root:

```bash
cd impl
pip install -e .[dev]
# Replace <adapter> with the adapter you're contributing (e.g., entra-id):
pytest tests/integration/test_<adapter>_tier1.py -v
```

A successful tier-1 run produces:

1. Test exit code 0.
2. An OSCAL evidence bundle written under `impl/out/tier1/<adapter>/<timestamp>/`.
3. An auto-generated contract fixture candidate under `tests/fixtures/contract/<adapter>/<operation>.yaml` — raw request/response pairs ready to become tier-2 fixtures after review and sanitization.

**Verify:** commit the sanitized fixture (with all tenant IDs / user principals replaced by placeholder tokens like `<TENANT_ID>`, `<USER_PRINCIPAL>`) in a canon PR that advances the adapter's registry `status` from `draft` → `alpha` (tier-2 green achievable) or `alpha` → `beta` (tier-1 + tier-2 green).

## Renewal

The Developer Program subscription lasts **90 days** and renews automatically on qualified developer activity (e.g., running tests against it, making Graph calls). If you stop using it for 90 days, it expires. A calendar reminder at day 60 to run `pytest tests/integration/` once is enough to maintain it.

## Using a Federal GCC-Moderate tenant

The steps above also work against a **Federal GCC-Moderate tenant** — with the differences below. There is no developer program for GCC-Moderate: Microsoft gates sign-up behind government eligibility validation, so the tenant is always **provided by an agency or a government-serving organization**, never self-provisioned. This section is for contributors who already have (or can be granted) authorized access to one.

::: {.callout-important}
## Authorization first
A GCC-Moderate tenant is a federal boundary. Before touching it: **written authorization** from the tenant owner naming you, the scope, and the time window; a **non-production** tenant only; and every credential handled under the agency's policy, not just this page's. UIAO's CI infrastructure never holds federal credentials ([UIAO_131 §3.3](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/specs/adapter-test-strategy.md)) — anything you capture runs from inside the agency's boundary, under its rules.
:::

### What changes, step by step

| Step | Developer Program (commercial) | Federal GCC-Moderate |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — Tenant | Self-serve, free, ~15 minutes | Agency-provided; eligibility-validated sign-up via Microsoft; licensing is G-SKU (e.g., G5) rather than E5 |
| 2 — App registration | You are the admin | Agency tenant admins create it (or delegate); app-registration creation is commonly restricted by policy |
| 3 — API permissions | You grant admin consent | Agency Global Administrator grants consent; expect a change-control step |
| 4 — Client secret | 90-day secret is fine | Follow agency credential policy; prefer certificate auth ([UIAO_129 §2](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/specs/application-identity-model.md)) |
| 5–6 — Endpoints | `login.microsoftonline.com` / `graph.microsoft.com` | **Identical.** GCC-Moderate rides the WW Commercial endpoints — see below |
| 7 — Evidence | Tier-1 fixtures, `-commercial` naming | Live `-gcc-moderate` fixture capture and, via the reference-deployment program, tier-3 evidence |

### Endpoints: same hosts, different boundary

GCC-Moderate uses the **same** sign-in and Graph hosts as WW Commercial — `https://login.microsoftonline.com` and `https://graph.microsoft.com`. In UIAO's sovereign-cloud resolver (`uiao.adapters._graph_clouds`), the `commercial` cloud entry serves GCC-Moderate too; only GCC-High (`graph.microsoft.us`) and DoD (`dod-graph.microsoft.us`) use different hosts, and those are outside UIAO scope per ADR-028. So the token-flow verification in Step 6 works unchanged against a GCC-Moderate tenant — no endpoint configuration differs. What differs is **feature availability inside the boundary**, which is exactly what the capture below documents.

### What a GCC-Moderate run buys the substrate

1. **Live `-gcc-moderate` tier-2 fixtures.** The contract fixtures under `tests/fixtures/contract/entra-id/` and `tests/fixtures/contract/m365/` that carry the `-gcc-moderate` suffix are today authored from Microsoft Learn citations. A live capture upgrades their provenance from `microsoft-learn` to `live-capture` (sanitized per `tests/fixtures/contract/README.md`, with agency consent recorded in the provenance block, and `cloud_variant: [gcc-moderate]` set).
2. **Confirmation (or refutation) of documented findings.** The [findings register](../findings/index.html) carries a family of GCC-Moderate boundary findings — FINDING-001 (Informed Network Routing unavailable), FINDING-003 (Adoption Score unavailable), FINDING-004 (Endpoint Analytics Advanced inferred unavailable), FINDING-005 (Entra Identity Protection ML risk scoring inferred blocked), among others. Several are *inferred* from documentation; a live run converts inference to observation, either way.
3. **Tier-3 evidence.** A run against an agency's non-production GCC-Moderate tenant under the reference-deployment program ([UIAO_131 §3.3](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/specs/adapter-test-strategy.md)) — gated on a named agency, point of contact, and scope agreement — produces the signed OSCAL evidence bundle that advances an adapter `beta → active`. That is the only path to `active`; commercial tier-1 tests deliberately do not count ([UIAO_131 §3.1](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/specs/adapter-test-strategy.md)).

### What a GCC-Moderate tenant does **not** replace

A GCC-Moderate tenant is a complement to the Developer Program tenant, not a substitute. Tier-1 conformance runs stay on the commercial developer tenant — it is disposable, renewable, and holds no federal data, which is what makes nightly CI against it acceptable. Keep both: commercial for iteration speed, GCC-Moderate for boundary truth.

## Alternate vendors (when not testing Microsoft adapters)

| Adapter | Alternate tier-1 target | Sign-up |
|---|---|---|
| `service-now` | [ServiceNow Developer Program](https://developer.servicenow.com/) — free personal instance, hibernates on idle | Developer Program sign-up |
| `cyberark` | CyberArk developer program — identity/vault eval | Vendor site |
| `palo-alto` | Beacon / eval programs | Vendor site |
| `terraform` | Local tfstate fixtures — no tenant required | No sign-up |
| `scuba` / `scubagear` | CISA open-source, local run against M365 Dev tenant above | No separate sign-up |
| `infoblox` / `bluecat-address-manager` | **Tier-1 blocked** — vendor sales contact only (see [UIAO_131 §5.1](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/specs/adapter-test-strategy.md) and [FINDING candidates in docs/findings/](../findings/index.html)) |
